mainTopic: Knots on שבת (robe, hairnet, shoe and sandal straps) and the status of a torn sandal for שבת, טומאה, and חליצה
overview: This amud continues the גמרא's explanation of the משנה about tying knots on שבת. It sets out three levels: knots that carry a חיוב חטאת, knots that are פטור אבל אסור (a camel's nose ring, a ship's ring), and knots that are מותר לכתחילה (a robe opening). The גמרא asks 'פשיטא!' about the robe opening and the hairnet strings, and shows the חידוש in each. In each case, a knot that looks like it might stay tied forever is really untied regularly. Three ברייתות on untying shoe and sandal straps seem to contradict each other. The גמרא solves this by matching each ruling to a different kind of knot, depending on how long it is meant to last. The story of רב יהודה's sandals, shared with his child, shows אביי changing his ruling once he learns the knot is retied all the time. Next come two stories about a torn sandal strap on שבת: רבי אבהו allows a fix, and רב יוסף forbids handling the sandal. רב יוסף explains the difference and rests on the view of רבי יהודה. The גמרא then analyzes רבי יוחנן's statement about a broken sandal for טומאה, שבת, and חליצה, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Knots with no liability but still prohibited
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives examples of the משנה's middle category: knots on a camel's nose ring and a ship's ring carry no חיוב חטאת, but they are still אסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: A knot tied to a camel's nose ring and a knot tied to a ship's ring: there is no liability for a sin-offering, but there is a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains which knots the משנה means when it says some knots carry no liability. Examples are the camel-ring knot and the ship-ring knot, which are exempt but still forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These knots are not permanent enough to be the full Torah-level מלאכה of קושר, so you do not bring a חטאת. But they last long enough that the חכמים still forbade tying them. This sets up a three-level scale: liable, exempt but prohibited, and fully permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: A ring at the front of a ship

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'פטור אבל אסור' (exempt but prohibited) is a key category across הלכות שבת. It is also the exact wording that comes back in step 7.

phrases.english: A knot that they tie to a camel's nose ring
and a knot that they tie to a ship's ring,
it is liability that there is not,
but a prohibition, there is.

steps.triggerLanguage: חִיּוּבָא הוּא דְּלֵיכָּא, הָא אִיסּוּרָא אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of the משנה's categories of knots from the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Knots on a camel's nose ring or a ship's ring: פטור from a חטאת but אסור.

steps.title: Knots permitted from the start: the robe opening
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the third category, knots that are מותר לכתחילה, with the example of a woman tying the opening of her robe.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there are knots that are permitted from the start. Which are they? She ties the openings of her robe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the fully permitted category of knots. It asks 'which are they?' and answers with the woman's robe opening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This knot is tied and untied every day, so it is not permanent at all. That is why it is not even rabbinically forbidden. The phrase 'ומאי ניהו' is just a quick internal question to present the example.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start; you may do it even at the outset
The neck opening of her robe

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels of knots: Torah-level חיוב; פטור אבל אסור (camel ring, ship ring); and מותר לכתחילה (robe opening).

phrases.english: And there are some that are permitted from the start,
and what are they?
She ties the openings of her robe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of categories by adding the fully permitted level.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tying the robe opening is מותר לכתחילה.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need to permit the robe opening?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of the robe opening and objects: 'פשיטא!' This is obvious, since that knot is clearly temporary.
steps.simpleTranslation: The opening of her robe: this is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'the opening of her robe' and challenges why the משנה even had to say it. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A knot that is opened every day is obviously not permanent, so permitting it seems to teach nothing. The challenge forces the גמרא to find a case where the הלכה is a real חידוש.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (Why did the משנה need to say this?)

phrases.english: "The opening of her robe." It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from listing the categories to examining a specific case in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's need to state that tying the robe opening is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The knot is plainly temporary, so the ruling seems to add nothing new.

steps.title: A robe with two laces
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is needed for a robe with two laces. You might think she only unties one and the other becomes permanent, so the משנה teaches that both are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only where the robe has two laces. You might have said that she leaves one of them unused (never untying it), so the משנה teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חידוש is about a robe with two ties. One might think she only ever uses one, which would make the other a permanent knot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that she can slip the robe off by opening just one lace, so the second knot would stay tied forever. The משנה teaches that she does untie both, so neither knot counts as permanent.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only (for a special case)
She sets it aside and leaves it unused

phrases.aramaic: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאִית לֵיהּ תְּרֵי דַשֵּׁי.
phrases.english: It is only necessary where it has two laces.
You might have said:
one of them she leaves unused (never untied),
it teaches us (that this is not so).

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאִית לֵיהּ תְּרֵי דַשֵּׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'פשיטא' challenge by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With two laces, one would be left permanently tied, making it a forbidden permanent knot.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both laces are untied, so neither is permanent and both are permitted.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need to permit hairnet strings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of the hairnet strings and again objects that this is obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the strings of a hairnet: this is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next permitted case, the hairnet strings, and asks why the משנה needed to say it. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hairnet is put on and taken off regularly, so its knot looks clearly temporary. The challenge follows the same pattern as the robe case.

phrases.english: "And the strings of a hairnet." It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same 'פשיטא' challenge to the next case in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's need to state that tying the hairnet strings is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The hairnet knot is obviously temporary, so the ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: A loose hairnet: a woman protects her hair
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is needed for a loose hairnet that could be slipped off without untying. It teaches that a woman cares for her hair, so she will untie it anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only where the net is loose on her. You might have said she slips it off (leaving the knot in place). So the משנה teaches us that a woman is protective of her hair, and she unties it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the case is a loose hairnet. One might think she just pulls it off and the knot stays tied forever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she pulled it off without untying, the knot would be permanent and forbidden. The משנה teaches that a woman does not want to pull out her hair, so she unties the net. That keeps the knot temporary.

keyTerms.meaning: She is protective of her hair

steps.whatToRemember: In both cases, the robe and the hairnet, the חידוש is that a knot one might think stays tied forever is really untied regularly, so it is not a permanent knot.

phrases.english: It is only necessary where it is loose on her.
You might have said: she slips it off (without untying),

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּאִשָּׁה חָסָה עַל שְׂעָרָהּ
phrases.english: it teaches us that a woman is protective of her hair
and so she unties it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'פשיטא' challenge about hairnet strings.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case narrowing (לא צריכא) plus a behavioral assumption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A loose net is slipped off whole, so its knot would be permanent.
steps.terutzMaskana: A woman unties it to protect her hair, so the knot is temporary and permitted.

steps.title: Three conflicting rulings on untying shoe and sandal straps
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's case of shoe and sandal straps, the גמרא brings three ברייתות about untying them: חייב חטאת, פטור אבל אסור, and מותר לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the straps of a shoe and sandal. It was stated: one who unties the straps of a shoe or sandal. One ברייתא taught: he is liable to a sin-offering. Another taught: he is exempt but it is prohibited. Another taught: it is permitted from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of shoe and sandal straps and lays out three ברייתות that disagree. This sets up the contradiction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three rulings match the three levels of knots seen in steps 1 and 2. Each ברייתא seems to put the very same act at a different level, from Torah liability down to fully permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: The straps of a shoe and a sandal

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה talks about tying (קושר) the straps, but these ברייתות talk about untying (מתיר). The same rules apply to both, since untying a permanent knot is also a מלאכה.

phrases.english: "And the straps of a shoe and a sandal."
It was stated: one who untied the straps of a shoe or sandal,
one baraita taught: he is liable to a sin-offering,
and another taught: he is exempt but it is prohibited,
and another taught: it is permitted from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next case in the משנה and introduces outside sources about it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three ברייתות give three different rulings on untying shoe and sandal straps.

steps.title: Shoe contradicts shoe, sandal contradicts sandal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתות contradict each other: one ruling on a shoe conflicts with another ruling on a shoe, and the same is true for sandals.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difficulty: shoe against shoe. There is a difficulty: sandal against sandal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the problem outright. The sources give opposite rulings about the very same item, a shoe or a sandal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קשיא is set up in pairs, shoe against shoe and sandal against sandal. This hints that the answer will divide the cases within each item, rather than simply contrasting shoes with sandals. Steps 9 and 10 give the גמרא's resolution.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult (there is a contradiction)

phrases.english: It is difficult: shoe against shoe,
it is difficult: sandal against sandal.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא מִנְעָל אַמִּנְעָל, קַשְׁיָא סַנְדָּל אַסַּנְדָּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the contradiction among the three ברייתות just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The three ברייתות on untying shoe and sandal straps.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same act on the same item cannot be both liable, exempt-but-forbidden, and fully permitted.

steps.title: Three kinds of shoe knots answer the shoe contradiction
steps.stepSummary: Each shoe ruling refers to a different kind of knot: a shoemaker's knot, the loose knot of the Sages, and the daily knot of the people of מחוזא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The shoe ruling against the other shoe ruling is not a problem. The one that says 'liable for a חטאת' is talking about a shoemaker's knot. 'Exempt but forbidden' is talking about the shoes of the Sages. 'Permitted from the start' is talking about the people of מחוזא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the shoe contradiction from Step 8. Each of the three ברייתות is talking about a different kind of shoe knot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: How bad the act is depends on how long the knot is meant to last. A shoemaker's knot holds the shoe together for good, so tying it is a real מלאכה. The Sages tie loosely and sometimes leave the knot in place, so it is only forbidden מדרבנן. The fussy people of מחוזא tie and untie every day, so their knot is not lasting at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Of the Sages. Here it means the loosely tied shoes that Torah scholars wear.
The people of the city of מחוזא, known for being careful about how they dress
It is not difficult. This phrase opens a resolution.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main rule for the whole section. The law of tying depends on how permanent the knot is, not on the object being tied.

phrases.english: Shoe against shoe is not difficult:
that one which teaches 'liable for a sin-offering'
refers to the knot of shoemakers.
phrases.notes: A permanent knot that holds the shoe together.

phrases.english: 'Exempt but forbidden'
refers to the shoes of the Sages.
phrases.notes: They tie loosely so they can slip the shoes on and off.

phrases.english: 'Permitted from the outset'
refers to the shoes of the people of Mechoza.
phrases.notes: They tie and untie every day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the shoe half of the contradiction raised in Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different kind of knot
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All three ברייתות seemed to rule on the same kind of shoe knot.
steps.terutzMaskana: Permanent shoemaker's knot = חייב חטאת. Sages' loose knot = פטור אבל אסור. מחוזא daily knot = מותר לכתחילה.

steps.title: Three kinds of sandal knots answer the sandal contradiction
steps.stepSummary: Each sandal ruling refers to a different case: Arab sandals tied by shoemakers, straps tied by ordinary people, and a sandal shared by two people.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sandal ruling against the other sandal ruling is not a problem. 'Liable for a חטאת' is talking about Arab sandals that shoemakers tie. 'Exempt but forbidden' is talking about straps that people tie themselves. 'Permitted from the start' is talking about a sandal that two people take turns wearing, like the case of רב יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the sandal contradiction in the same way it answered the shoe contradiction. It ends by pointing to a story about רב יהודה, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, the ruling depends on how lasting the knot is. A shoemaker's knot on an Arab sandal is permanent. A knot an ordinary person ties may stay for a while. When two people share one sandal, the strap must be retied to fit each of them, so the knot never lasts.

keyTerms.meaning: Arabs. Here it means Arab-style sandals.
Two people go out wearing it, taking turns

phrases.english: Sandal against sandal is not difficult:
that one which teaches 'liable for a sin-offering'
refers to Arab sandals, which shoemakers tie.
'Exempt but forbidden'
refers to straps that they themselves tie.
phrases.notes: These are ordinary people, not professionals.

phrases.english: 'Permitted from the outset'
refers to a sandal that two people go out in,
like the case of Rav Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the sandal half of the contradiction from Step 8, using the same method as Step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All three sandal rulings seemed to address the same kind of strap.
steps.terutzMaskana: Arab sandals with shoemaker's knot = חייב חטאת. Self-tied straps = פטור אבל אסור. Shared sandal = מותר לכתחילה.

steps.title: רב יהודה asks אביי about his shared sandals
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה shared a pair of sandals with his child and asked אביי about tying them on שבת. אביי first said he would be חייב חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה, the brother of רב סלא חסידא, had a pair of sandals. Sometimes he wore them and sometimes his child wore them. He came before אביי and asked: in a case like this, what is the law? אביי told him: you are liable for a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the story behind the case of the shared sandal. אביי's first answer is very strict, and that sets up רב יהודה's surprised reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי seems to have treated the strap as an ordinary lasting knot, so tying it would be a full Torah-level מלאכה. He did not yet know how often the strap was retied.

keyTerms.meaning: רב סלא the pious. רב יהודה in this story is his brother.
In a case like this, what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אֲחוּהּ דְּרַב סַלָּא חֲסִידָא
phrases.english: For Rav Yehuda, the brother of Rav Sala the Pious,
had a certain pair of sandals;
sometimes he would go out in them,
sometimes his child would go out in them.
He came before Abaye
and said to him: In a case like this, what is the law?
He said to him: You are liable for a sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אֲחוּהּ דְּרַב סַלָּא חֲסִידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells the story that Step 10 pointed to with the words כדרב יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי's first ruling: tying the shared sandal makes one חייב חטאת.

steps.title: רב יהודה is surprised by the strict ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה objects: even calling it פטור אבל אסור would be hard for me to accept, and you say חייב חטאת?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said to him: Even if you had said 'exempt but forbidden,' that would already be hard for me. And you tell me 'liable for a חטאת'?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה pushes back against אביי's ruling. He feels it is far too strict for his situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה does not explain his reason yet. He only says that his case seems to deserve no prohibition at all, so a full Torah-level liability makes no sense to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Now. Here it means: even the lighter ruling would be hard, so all the more so this one.
You are telling me?! (said in surprise)

phrases.english: He said to him: Now,

phrases.aramaic: פָּטוּר אֲבָל אָסוּר קָא קַשְׁיָא לִי,
phrases.english: even 'exempt but forbidden' would be difficult for me,
and you tell me 'liable for a sin-offering'?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא פָּטוּר אֲבָל אָסוּר קָא קַשְׁיָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's ruling from Step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר argument (signaled by הַשְׁתָּא): if even the lighter ruling of פטור אבל אסור seems wrong, the heavier ruling of חייב חטאת surely does.

steps.title: אביי asks for the reason
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks: why does even a rabbinic prohibition seem wrong to you?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks רב יהודה to explain his objection. This sets up רב יהודה's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי is checking which facts he may have missed. He wants to know what makes this case different from a normal sandal knot.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of רב יהודה's objection in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What fact about the sandals makes even a rabbinic prohibition seem wrong?

steps.title: The sandals are retied all the time, even on weekdays
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that on weekdays too, he and his child take turns wearing the sandals.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because on weekdays too, sometimes I go out in them and sometimes the child goes out in them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives the missing fact. The strap is untied and retied all the time, every day of the week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An adult foot and a child's foot need different fittings. So the knot is changed constantly and is never meant to stay. A knot like that is not lasting at all.

phrases.english: He said to him: Because on weekdays too,
sometimes I go out in them,
sometimes the child goes out in them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question from Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The knot is constantly retied for different wearers, so it is never a lasting knot.

steps.title: אביי rules it is fully permitted
steps.stepSummary: Once he hears the facts, אביי rules that tying the shared sandal is מותר לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If so, it is permitted from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי changes his ruling based on the new fact. This closes the story and confirms the third category from Step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The facts changed the category completely. אביי moved from the most severe level, חייב חטאת, to fully allowed, because a knot that is retied all the time is not a 'tying' at all.
steps.whatToRemember: For knots on שבת, everything depends on how long the knot is meant to last. Permanent = חייב חטאת. Sometimes left in place = פטור אבל אסור. Retied regularly = מותר לכתחילה.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי did not change his mind about the law. He learned new facts about the case. The same rule applied to different facts gives a different result.

phrases.english: He said to him: If so,
it is permitted from the outset.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final ruling after hearing the facts in Step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A sandal shared by two people, whose knot is constantly retied, may be tied and untied on שבת from the start.

steps.title: רבי אבהו lets רבי ירמיה wrap a torn strap with a reed
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה's sandal strap tore in a כרמלית. רבי אבהו told him to wrap a moist reed fit for animal food around it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה was walking behind רבי אבהו in a כרמלית. The strap of his sandal tore. He asked: What should I do with it? רבי אבהו told him: Take a moist reed that is fit for animal food and wrap it around the sandal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic about a torn sandal strap on שבת. It starts with a lenient story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A moist reed is food for animals, so it is not מוקצה and may be handled. Wrapping it around the sandal is not a real knot. This lets רבי ירמיה keep wearing the sandal instead of leaving it behind or carrying it in the כרמלית.

keyTerms.meaning: An area that is neither fully public nor private. Carrying there is forbidden מדרבנן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya was walking
behind Rabbi Abbahu in a karmelit.
The strap of his sandal tore.
He said to him: What should I do with it?
He said to him: Take a moist reed
that is fit for animal food,
and wrap it around it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה הֲוָה קָאָזֵיל בָּתְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new related topic: what to do with a torn sandal strap on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a כרמלית, one may wrap a torn sandal with a moist reed fit for animal food.

steps.title: רב יוסף tells אביי to leave his torn sandal
steps.stepSummary: אביי's strap tore while he stood before רב יוסף. רב יוסף told him to leave it alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי was standing before רב יוסף. His strap tore. He asked: What should I do with it? רב יוסף told him: Leave it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second story with the same problem but a stricter answer. This sets up the comparison that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף does not allow any fixing or even moving of the sandal. This seems to clash with רבי אבהו's lenient answer in the story just told.

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי הֲוָה קָאֵי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף.
phrases.english: Abaye was standing before Rav Yosef.
His strap tore.
He said to him: What should I do with it?
He said to him: Leave it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי הֲוָה קָאֵי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story with a stricter ruling than Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף: leave the torn sandal and do not handle it.

steps.title: אביי asks why his case differs from Rabbi Yirmeya's
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף: how is this different from the case of רבי ירמיה, who was allowed to fix his sandal?
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this different from the case of רבי ירמיה?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי points out that the two stories seem to contradict each other. He asks רב יוסף to explain the difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases involve a torn sandal strap on שבת. So it seems they should get the same ruling.

phrases.english: What is different from the case of Rabbi Yirmeya?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's ruling in Step 17 using the story in Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's instruction to leave the sandal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction with a precedent: רבי אבהו was lenient in the same situation.

steps.title: There it would be lost, here it is safe
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains: in a כרמלית the sandal would not be safe, but here it is safe where it lies.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it would not be guarded. Here, it is guarded.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains the difference between the two stories. It depends on whether the sandal would be lost if left behind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה was out in a כרמלית, where a sandal left behind would be lost. So the Sages allowed a gentle fix to save it. אביי was in a safe place, so there was no loss to prevent and no reason to allow handling it.

phrases.english: There, it was not guarded;
here, it is guarded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question from Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases: the risk of loss
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both torn-sandal cases should get the same ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: Leniency is given only where the sandal would otherwise be lost.

steps.title: But the sandal is still a usable utensil
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects: the torn sandal is still a כלי, since I could switch it from the right foot to the left foot and wear it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is still a utensil, since if I want, I can switch it from the right foot to the left foot!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges again. He argues that the torn sandal is still usable, so it should not be מוקצה and he should be allowed to move it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sandal is turned to the other foot, the torn side might still be wearable. If it is still a working כלי, it may be moved on שבת whether or not it is safe.

keyTerms.meaning: I can turn or switch it

phrases.english: But it is a utensil,
for if I want, I can switch it
from right to left?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind רב יוסף's ruling that the torn sandal may not be handled.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the torn sandal is not a usable כלי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since it can still be worn on the other foot, it is still a כלי and may be moved.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that since רבי יוחנן explains a source according to רבי יהודה, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. According to him, a torn sandal does not count as a כלי just because it could be switched.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Since רבי יוחנן explains the matter according to רבי יהודה, learn from this that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי's challenge by relying on the view of רבי יהודה. The גמרא will explain this view further.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, the fact that the sandal could be switched to the other foot does not keep it a usable כלי. רב יוסף proves the הלכה follows רבי יהודה because רבי יוחנן went out of his way to explain a source according to him. So the torn sandal may not be handled.
steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף does not quote רבי יהודה's actual ruling here. Steps 22 through 29 quote the source and work out the reasoning.

phrases.english: He said to him: Since Rabbi Yochanan explains the matter
according to the view of Rabbi Yehuda,
learn from this that the halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָמְתָרֵץ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeal to a halachic ruling based on an inference from רבי יוחנן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A sandal that could be switched to the other foot is still a usable כלי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה, so the torn sandal is not treated as a כלי because of that possibility.

steps.title: Which ruling of רבי יהודה is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what source רב יוסף was referring to when he said רבי יוחנן explains a ruling according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is that source?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next step. It wants to know which source רב יוסף meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21, רב יוסף said the halacha follows רבי יהודה because רבי יוחנן explains a source according to him. He did not say which source. This question opens the door to quoting it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (asks for the source being referred to)

phrases.english: What is it?
phrases.notes: He's asking where רב יוסף's claim back in step 21 comes from.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source mentioned in רב יוסף's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which teaching of רבי יהודה, explained by רבי יוחנן, is being referred to.

steps.title: The ברייתא about a broken sandal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules on when a broken sandal becomes טהור. רבי יהודה disagrees about a sandal with only one torn strap.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: if a sandal's two ears broke, or its two straps, or its whole sole was removed, it is טהור. If only one ear or one strap broke, or only most of the sole was removed, it is still טמא. רבי יהודה says: if the inner strap broke, it is still טמא. If the outer strap broke, it is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source: a ברייתא about when a broken sandal stops being a כלי and so becomes טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something that is no longer a usable כלי loses its טומאה. The תנא קמא says that if only one strap broke, the sandal is still a כלי, so it stays טמא. רבי יהודה says this depends on which strap broke. If the outer strap broke, the sandal is no longer a כלי, even though it could be switched to the other foot.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
The 'ears' or loops of the sandal that hold the straps

steps.confusionAlert: The question here is whether the sandal still counts as a כלי. When it says 'טהור,' it means the sandal is so broken that it is no longer a כלי, so it cannot hold טומאה.

phrases.english: As it was taught: a sandal whose two ears broke,
or its two straps,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁנִּיטַּל כׇּל הַכַּף שֶׁלּוֹ — טָהוֹר.
phrases.english: or whose entire sole was removed: it is pure.
If only one of its ears, or one of its straps, broke,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁנִּיטַּל רוֹב הַכַּף שֶׁלּוֹ — טָמֵא.
phrases.english: or most of its sole was removed: it is impure.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: נִפְסְקָה פְּנִימִית — טָמֵא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: if the inner strap broke, it is impure.
If the outer one broke, it is pure.
phrases.notes: For רבי יהודה, the sandal is no longer a כלי, even though it could be switched to the other foot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22 by quoting the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא on broken sandals, where רבי יהודה rules that a sandal with a torn outer strap is טהור.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the same dispute applies to שבת but not to חליצה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the dispute about טומאה also applies to שבת, but it does not apply to חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And עולא said, and some say רבה בר בר חנה said, that רבי יוחנן said: just as there is a dispute about טומאה, there is the same dispute about שבת, but not about חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן extends the ברייתא's dispute. It also decides whether you may wear such a sandal on שבת. He says it has no bearing on חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sandal is still a כלי, you may wear it on שבת. If it is not a כלי, wearing it is like carrying. So the טומאה dispute carries over to שבת. רבי יוחנן says חליצה works differently, but he does not explain how. That is what the next steps will work out.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (gives an alternate name for who reported it)
The ceremony of removing the brother-in-law's shoe (instead of יבום)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the statement רב יוסף relied on in step 21 to say the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר עוּלָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
phrases.english: And Ulla said, and some say Rabba bar bar Ḥana,
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Just like the dispute with regard to impurity,
so too is there a dispute with regard to Shabbat,
but not with regard to ḥalitza.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר עוּלָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רבי יוחנן's statement about the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The טומאה dispute about a torn sandal also applies to שבת, but not to חליצה.

steps.title: Which view does רבי יוחנן follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יוחנן's statement follows רבנן or רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: according to whom is רבי יוחנן speaking?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up an investigation: whose view is רבי יוחנן explaining? It will now test each option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'but not for חליצה' could be read two ways, depending on whose view they follow. The גמרא will try each reading and look for problems.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (introduces an earlier discussion)

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
According to whom is Rabbi Yoḥanan speaking?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts analyzing רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יוחנן follows רבנן or רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Following רבנן clashes with the משנה about a left shoe on the right foot
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוחנן follows רבנן, he would be saying the sandal is not a כלי for חליצה. But a משנה says חליצה with a left shoe on the right foot is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he follows רבנן: since it is a כלי for טומאה, it is also a כלי for שבת, but not for חליצה, where it is not a כלי. But we learned in a משנה: if she removed a left shoe that was on the right foot, her חליצה is valid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries reading רבי יוחנן according to רבנן, then attacks that reading with a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, the sandal counts as a כלי for טומאה and שבת because it can be switched to the other foot. But it would not count for חליצה. Yet the משנה says a shoe worn on the wrong foot is still good for חליצה. So switching feet should not disqualify it there either.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in a משנה?

phrases.english: If you say it follows the Rabbis:
since with regard to impurity it is a utensil,
with regard to Shabbat it is also a utensil,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא לַחֲלִיצָה — דְּלָאו מָנָא הוּא,
phrases.english: but not for ḥalitza, where it is not a utensil,
but didn't we learn:
if she removed a left shoe from the right foot,
her ḥalitza is valid?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first option from step 25 and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading רבי יוחנן according to רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says a shoe worn on the wrong foot is valid for חליצה. So a sandal that works only when switched to the other foot should also be valid.

steps.title: So רבי יוחנן must follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Instead, רבי יוחנן follows רבי יהודה: the sandal is not a כלי for טומאה or שבת, but it is a כלי for חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he follows רבי יהודה: since it is not a כלי for טומאה, it is also not a כלי for שבת. But it is different for חליצה, where it is a כלי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא switches to the other option: רבי יוחנן is explaining רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, a sandal with a torn outer strap is not a כלי for טומאה or שבת. The phrase 'but not for חליצה' now means it does count for חליצה. This seems to fit the משנה's rule that switched feet are fine for חליצה.

phrases.english: Rather, it follows Rabbi Yehuda:
since with regard to impurity it is not a utensil,

phrases.aramaic: לְעִנְיַן שַׁבָּת נָמֵי לָאו מָנָא הוּא,
phrases.english: with regard to Shabbat it is also not a utensil,
but not so for ḥalitza, where it is a utensil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the רבנן reading, the גמרא offers the רבי יהודה reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the statement to the other תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן follows רבנן and disqualifies the sandal for חליצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן follows רבי יהודה: the sandal is not a כלי for טומאה or שבת, but it is valid for חליצה.

steps.title: The משנה only applies to a shoe that is a real כלי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the משנה about a left shoe on the right foot deals with a usable shoe. For רבי יהודה, this torn sandal is not a כלי at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that the rule 'if she removed a left shoe from the right foot, her חליצה is valid' applies only where the shoe is a כלי for its own use. Here it is not a כלי for its own use, as רבי יהודה said: if the outer strap tore, it is טהור. This shows it is not a כלי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the רבי יהודה reading. The משנה cannot prove that this torn sandal is valid for חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's left shoe is a real, working shoe that just happens to be on the wrong foot. רבי יהודה himself says a sandal with a torn outer strap is not a כלי at all. So why would it count for חליצה? Now both readings of רבי יוחנן seem to have a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Say that we said (limits a rule to a narrower case)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different cases here. A good shoe worn on the wrong foot is still a shoe. A sandal that only works when you switch it to the other foot is, for רבי יהודה, not a real shoe at all.

phrases.english: Say that we said

phrases.aramaic: חָלְצָה שֶׁל שְׂמֹאל בַּיָּמִין חֲלִיצָתָהּ כְּשֵׁרָה —
phrases.english: 'if she removed a left shoe from the right foot, her ḥalitza is valid'
only where it is a utensil for its own purpose;
here it is not a utensil for its own purpose,
for Rabbi Yehuda said:
if the outer strap tore, it is pure;
this shows it is not a utensil!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that, for רבי יהודה, the torn sandal is valid for חליצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה deals only with a shoe that is a real כלי. רבי יהודה rules that this sandal is not a כלי, so the משנה does not support using it for חליצה.

steps.title: Change the wording: 'and the same for חליצה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא keeps the רבי יהודה reading but changes רבי יוחנן's words. The torn sandal is also invalid for חליצה. This teaches the limit of the משנה's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he follows רבי יהודה. Say instead: 'and the same is true for חליצה.' And this teaches us that when we say 'if she removed a left shoe from the right foot, her חליצה is valid,' that is only where...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing רבי יוחנן's statement from 'but not for חליצה' to 'and the same for חליצה.' The explanation continues into the next passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רבי יוחנן says that for רבי יהודה, the torn sandal is not a כלי for טומאה, for שבת, or for חליצה. The new wording teaches a limit on the משנה: a left shoe on the right foot is valid only in a certain kind of case. The text breaks off right at 'where...'

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead (introduces a change in wording)
And this is what it teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture so far: רבי יוחנן follows רבי יהודה. A sandal with a torn outer strap is not a כלי for טומאה, for שבת, or for חליצה. The משנה about a left shoe on the right foot applies only to a limited case, which the next line will explain.

phrases.english: Actually, it follows Rabbi Yehuda.
Say instead: 'and the same for ḥalitza.'
And this is what it teaches us:
that when we say
'if she removed a left shoe from the right foot,
her ḥalitza is valid,' that is only where...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה. אֵימָא: וְכֵן לַחֲלִיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 28 by changing רבי יוחנן's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Change in the wording of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן said 'but not for חליצה,' meaning the sandal is valid for חליצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן said 'and the same for חליצה': for רבי יהודה, the torn sandal is invalid for חליצה too, and the משנה's rule is limited to a narrower case.
